text:
Alex P: Heads-up — Arm partner reached out about a joint perf/W + throughput benchmark on their new SoC. They want a reproducible playbook we can run across our sample models and a short public figure for a joint announcement. Thoughts on scope? cc @Sabrina L @Nate R

Sabrina L: Love it. Suggest we pick 3 representative workloads: chat (gpt-like), seq2seq (summarization), and embeddings. Metrics: throughput (toks/s), latency (p50/p95/p99), and perf/W (mJ/token). Keep public numbers aggregated.

Jordan H: Agree. Need to lock the measurement harness. Propose using our loadgen v2 (continuous batching) + power telemetry from the board PMIC. Also capture kernel config and toolchain. @BenchmarkBot can you spin up a sheet?

BenchmarkBot: Created sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Xx-example-link - columns: hw_id, firmware, model, batch, seq_len, perfW_mJ_per_token, throughput_toks_per_s, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kernel_flags, notes

Nate R: For kernel tuning, we'll need the partner to share their kernel build matrix and any vendor-specific compiler flags. With Arm it's not nvcc — more like platform SDK + JIT config. I'll ask them for a minimal reproducible image and a remote account. Also need to confirm power sampling interface (I2C PMIC vs external power meter).

Alex P: Partner can provide 2 dev boards and remote access for a 72-hour window. They also asked for a short marketing-friendly figure: "Redwood x Arm — efficiency at scale" showing perf/W vs throughput. Legal review needed for wording. @Kira (legal)

Kira (legal): High-level numbers and plots are fine. No raw logs, serials, or customer data in public materials. If partner requests per-board breakdown we need an NDA amendment. I'll draft a one-paragraph ok.

Sabrina L: Measurement plan (proposed): run each config for 15 minutes after a 10-minute warmup; sample power at 5 Hz; run FP16 and int8/quantized variants where supported; collect KV cache hit stats and token-level timing. Use same prompt mix across models. We'll include standard deviation and replicate runs (n=3) for stability.

Jordan H: Quick example command for the harness:
```
./loadgen --model gpt-small --batch 8 --seq 512 --duration 900 --warmup 600 --telemetry /tmp/power.csv --kv-stats /tmp/kv.json
```
Make sure to pin model sha and runtime kernel hash in the sheet.

Alex P: Timeline: partner wants initial numbers in 3 weeks for a joint blog and marketplace listing. Is that feasible? @Nate R @Sabrina L

Nate R: 3 weeks is tight but doable if remote access and image come this week. I'll prepare the kernel tuning matrix and list of required artifacts: toolchain version, dtb, firmware, kernel config, and power sampling endpoint.

BenchmarkBot: Uploaded initial artifacts to s3://redwood-benches/arm-soc-2026/ — will auto-populate runs under folder `drafts/` as they complete.

Sabrina L: I'll start drafting the methods and a short blurb for marketing. Alex, can you set a 30-min cross-functional sync tomorrow (marketing + partner + eng)? We should also block a 2-hour bench day once remote access is live.

Alex P: Will set the sync for tomorrow 10am PT and invite partner. Thanks everyone — let's keep the runbook simple and reproducible. :thumbsup:
